feedback_request.compare_against: Iteration 2 (16 mm, y = 0.04) and baseline iteration 0.

intent: Change one thing from the iteration 2 design: move all five sensors forward from y = 0.04 to y = 0.07 m, keeping the 0.16 m spread (x = -0.08, -0.04, 0, 0.04, 0.08), 16 mm footprints and the 25 times x sensor weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2). Integrator: keep kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0 and last_direction recovery, with no gain change. Expected result: line_loss_events stay near 0 on the oval, max_error falls below the 0.06 floor, and oval progress rises above 0.19 with lower steering_oscillation. If progress does not rise, the next step is gains, not geometry.
learning: Hypothesis A: a forward lead of 0.07 m gives the controller enough time to correct before the robot leaves the line, so max_error falls below the floor and progress rises. Hypothesis B: the lead change makes the signal lead too much and causes oscillation (steering_oscillation above about 0.10 on the oval). If A holds, next consider a 0.08 m lead. If B holds, reduce the lead or the Integrator should lower kd. Please report per-track progress and max_error, since the slalom and oval may respond differently.
rationale: Race evidence so far: iteration 0 (12 mm sensors, 0.04 m spacing) lost the line 2.15 times per oval run. Iteration 1 (0.03 m spacing, narrower spread) removed those losses but cut progress on every track (oval 0.19 to 0.115). Iteration 2 (16 mm sensors, 0.04 m spacing, baseline spread) also removed oval line losses (0.0) but progress stayed at 0.115 on the oval and slalom progress was 0.03. Max_error sat at the 0.06 m off-track floor in every race, and rms_error stayed near 0.03. So the footprint fixed the line-loss cause, but the robot still drifts off the line at its worst points, and narrowing the spread did not help. Iteration 2 also showed that the spacing and footprint changes alone do not explain the lost progress. The remaining candidate is late steering: the sensors sit only 0.04 m ahead of the axle, so the corrective signal arrives after the robot has already drifted. The Integrator's feedback in iteration 1 pointed the same way (slalom progress lost early with no line losses). This iteration keeps the iteration 2 footprint, which removed line losses, and moves the sensors forward to y = 0.07 to add steering lead. The spread stays at the baseline 0.16 m, and the weights stay at 25 times x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so steering gain per metre is unchanged. Wheel track, mass, radius and body are unchanged, so this race isolates the lead change. Expected result: oval and slalom line losses stay at zero, max_error drops below the 0.06 floor, and progress rises above 0.19 on the oval. If progress does not rise, the limit is controller lag or base speed, and the Integrator should tune gains rather than geometry.
